title: Rollout Orchestra: Handoff Cues & Observability Playlist (Draft)
content:
Purpose:
This is a compact, operational-facing draft for the next micro-rollout window. It focuses on: (1) concise handoff cues for on-call/shift leads, (2) an observability "playlist" of signals to monitor during the ramp, and (3) a short release-notes skeleton to copy into customer-facing notes. Treat as working — lots of TODOs and inline questions.

High-level summary:
- Release tag: release/2025-03-mixtape
- Primary change: switch default KV cache eviction policy + model kernel update (v2-infer-aug)
- Targeted regions: us-west1 -> staggered to eu-west1 after 60m if green
- Rollout type: progressive 0% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% (auto-step with telemetry gate)
- Owners: rollout lead: Asha P., SRE lead: Liam C., Observability: Maya O., Runtime eng: Evan Z.

Rollout timeline (compact):
- T-72h: Final smoke checklist & merge window (PR #987 merged)
- T-24h: Preflight snapshot (tracing + canary toggles) — confirm artifact hashes
- T-1h: Warmup scripts: kv-cache priming, small-batch synthetic traces (10m)
- T+0: 0% traffic flip to blue (canary cohort)
- T+60m: Evaluate metrics; auto-step to 5% if gates pass
- T+6h: Evaluate for region expansion to eu-west1 (manual approval)
- T+24h: Full ramp to 100% (or rollback if thresholds exceeded)

Handoff cues for shift leads (what to say in channel):
- "I’m the rollout lead for release/2025-03-mixtape. Starting canary now (0%). Observability playlist pinned. Ping me for manual expand"
- Key snapshots to post in channel: canary-smoke (trace id), p95-latency-scan, error-burst-sample
- Escalation: if any critical signal breaches, call SRE lead and pause expansion; open incident stub JIRA and attach logs.

Observability playlist (primary signals & quick checks) — sequence to run every 10m during first 2 hours, then every 30m:
1) Latency: generation_token_latency_p50/p95/p99 (per-model, per-region) — watch sudden skew vs baseline
2) Error rates: request_error_rate (4xx/5xx), model_decode_errors — alert threshold: >=2x baseline for 10m
3) Throughput & queuing: requests_per_minute, avg_queue_time_ms, batch_size_distribution
4) KV cache metrics: kv_cache_hit_ratio, eviction_rate — expected hit ratio delta +/- 3% during warmup
5) Cost & billing proxy: token_cost_estimate_per_minute (sampled) — watch spikes during escalations
6) Model fallback count: fallback_to_cpu_count and fallback_to-smaller-model_count
7) Traces: sample 5 recent traces for p95 requests and scan for cross-service timeouts
8) Perf counters: GPU_util_pct, kernel_rejection_rate, memory_pressure_events
9) Synthetics: run preconfigured prompt set (smoke prompts) and diff outputs against baseline for quality regressions

Gating rules (auto/soft gates):
- Auto-step from 0% -> 5% if: p95 latency <= baseline + 15% AND request_error_rate <= baseline * 1.5 AND kv_cache_hit_ratio >= baseline - 5% over 60m
- Abort & rollback if: p99 latency spikes > 2x baseline sustained 15m OR request_error_rate > baseline*3 for 5m OR memory_pressure_events > 3
- Manual guard: region expansion to eu-west1 requires SRE lead sign-off and a green telemetry snapshot attached in channel

Quick smoke checklist (pre-merge & pre-flip):
- [ ] PR merged: runtime #987 — verified artifact SHA matches release notes
- [ ] Chaos knobs off for canary cohort (no forced CPU fallback)
- [ ] Tracing enabled (sampling 100% for canary)
- [ ] Synthetic smoke set uploaded to observability for auto-run
- [ ] Canary route configured in routing table and traffic policy pinned
- [ ] Rollback button verified and runbook URL posted in channel

Release notes skeleton (copy / paste into external notes):
- Title: March 2025 Inference Stability & Cache Policy Update
- Summary: This release updates the KV cache eviction policy to improve cold-start latency for short prompts and includes a model kernel update (v2-infer-aug) that reduces token-level CPU overhead. Customers may see improved p50 generation latency for multi-turn prompts.
- Impact: No API changes. Performance optimizations only; we anticipate transient latency during warmup for affected workloads.
- Rollout plan: Progressive rollouts across regions with telemetry gating. See our status page and contact support if you notice regressions.
- Contact: support@redwood.ai, SRE on-call

Post-release tasks (first 48h):
- 0–4h: Keep telemetry checks every 30m; log any drift with sample traces
- 4–24h: Export sample model outputs for quality verification; run full eval suite overnight
- 24–48h: Cost/reliability retrospective: collect token-cost deltas and model fallback counts and add to retro doc

Open questions / TODOs:
- Can we add a short-lived metric for per-request kernel selection time? (Evan Z.)
- Should we widen synthetic prompt set to include long context prompt (8k) before Region eu expansion? (Maya O.)
- Confirm customer-facing blurb with comms — is "improved cold-start" acceptable phrasing? (Product)

Appendix: quick play actions (if things go sideways)
- If p99 latency spikes: pause rollout immediately, switch canary back to previous model variant, trigger rollback runbook, and collect top 10 traces for the incident stub.
- If kv_cache hit ratio drops >10%: run cache-priming job (script: infra/cache/prime_canary.sh) and temporarily pause expansion until hit ratio recovers for 30m.
- If GPU kernel rejection increases: reduce concurrency on canary pool and increase autoscaler min instances; notify runtime team to investigate kernel mismatch.

Changelog for this draft:
- 2025-03-12 Asha: initial outline and timeline
- 2025-03-15 Maya: added observability playlist
- 2025-03-18 Liam: tightened gate numbers and added rollback triggers

Notes to self: keep this file short. Move detailed run commands to /runbooks/rollout-orchestra (linked) once stable.
